issue: No index on order.user; getMyOrders runs Order.find({ user }) on the hot path with a full collection scan
evidence: orderModel.js: `user: { type: ObjectId, ref: 'User' }` has no `index: true`; orderController.js:158 `Order.find({ user: req.user._id })`
estimated_impact: COLLSCAN on every GET /api/orders/myorders. At ~10k orders Mongo scans all docs: ~50-300ms p95 per call vs <2ms with an index; grows linearly with collection size, so +500ms-2s at 1M docs.
recommendation: Add `orderSchema.index({ user: 1, createdAt: -1 })`. Covers both the myorders filter and chronological sort.

issue: Keyword product search uses $regex with no index; every GET /api/products with a keyword is a full collection scan + per-doc regex
evidence: productController.js:20-23 `Product.countDocuments({ name: { $regex, $options:'i' } })` then `Product.find(...)`; productModel.js has no index on `name`
estimated_impact: Two full scans per request (countDocuments + find), each running a case-insensitive regex against every product name. A leading-wildcard/unanchored regex cannot use a btree index even if one existed. At 50k products: ~100-400ms p95; CPU-bound on the event loop. Cross-ref SEC-05 (ReDoS amplifies this into catastrophic backtracking).
recommendation: Add a MongoDB `$text` index on `name` (+`description`) and switch to `$text`/`$search`, or anchor + escape the regex. Cap keyword length. See SEC-05 for the security side.

issue: features.json (~14KB) is read from disk and JSON.parsed on EVERY feature-flag request; no caching despite the file changing rarely
evidence: featureFlagController.js:9-12 `readFeatures()` does `await readFile(FEATURES_PATH)` + `JSON.parse(raw)` on each call to getFeatureFlags and getFeatureFlag (server.js:31, public/unauthenticated per SEC-04)
estimated_impact: Per request: one filesystem syscall + a ~14KB JSON.parse (synchronous CPU, ~0.2-0.5ms event-loop block). On a public, unauthenticated endpoint this is a free amplification vector: 1k req/s = 1k disk reads/s + ~200-500ms/s of blocked event loop. The same pattern repeats in both MCP servers (search-docs is fine; feature-flags MCP reads the file on every tool call too).
recommendation: Load features once at module init and cache in memory; invalidate via fs.watch or on the write path (feature-flags MCP already owns writes). For the API, also add a short Cache-Control/ETag. Cross-ref SEC-04 (the endpoint should not be public at all).

issue: Admin getOrders and getMyOrders/getUsers return the ENTIRE collection with no limit/skip — unbounded payload and memory
evidence: orderController.js:166 `Order.find({}).populate('user','id name')`; orderController.js:158 `Order.find({ user })`; userController.js:111 `User.find({})` — none paginate
estimated_impact: Response and Mongo cursor size grow O(collection). At 100k orders each row carries an embedded orderItems array → multi-MB JSON serialized synchronously on the event loop (blocks ~tens of ms) and buffered fully in Node heap (+50-200MB transient). p95 degrades unboundedly; risk of OOM under admin load.
recommendation: Add the same pageSize/skip pagination already used in getProducts; cap with `.limit()` and return `{ items, page, pages }`. Select only needed fields.

issue: express.json() has no size limit; large request bodies are buffered and JSON-parsed synchronously on the event loop
evidence: server.js:25 `app.use(express.json())` — default 100KB but no explicit cap, applied globally including the public POST surfaces
estimated_impact: A large/maliciously crafted JSON body forces a synchronous parse that blocks the event loop for the parse duration (e.g. a deeply nested or large array body = tens of ms of 100% CPU, stalling all concurrent requests). Combined with the order-create path that maps over orderItems, an attacker-sized orderItems array multiplies the cost. Cross-ref SEC-14 (missing body-size cap / DoS).
recommendation: Set `express.json({ limit: '16kb' })` (tune per endpoint), and validate orderItems length before the map in addOrderItems.

issue: All 18 route screens (incl. admin dashboard + PayPal) are statically imported into one bundle; no code-splitting / React.lazy
evidence: App.js:6-22 eager `import HomeScreen ... FeatureFlagsScreen`; store.js:3 imports redux-devtools-extension's composeWithDevTools unconditionally; frontend/package.json ships react-paypal-button-v2 loaded eagerly via OrderScreen
estimated_impact: First-paint bundle includes admin-only screens (FeatureFlags table, AutoPilot), PayPal SDK wrapper, and devtools glue that a typical shopper never uses. On CRA 3.4.3 (no modern tree-shaking) this is easily +150-300KB gzipped → +300-600ms LCP on a 3G/mid-mobile connection. devtools-extension code also ships to prod.
recommendation: Code-split with React.lazy/Suspense per route (at minimum the /admin/* screens and OrderScreen's PayPal). Guard composeWithDevTools behind NODE_ENV !== 'production'. Lazy-load the PayPal button only when payment is reached.

issue: Reranker spawns a fresh Python process per query; the cross-encoder model is cold-loaded on every searchHybridReranked call
evidence: rerank.ts:19 `spawn(PYTHON_BIN, [RERANK_SCRIPT])` inside the per-query rerank() promise; hybrid-rerank.ts:48 awaits it after embed+qdrant
estimated_impact: Each reranked query pays Python interpreter startup + model load (sentence-transformers/cross-encoder typically 0.5-3s cold) on top of embed+retrieve. Throughput is capped at roughly one query / (process-spawn + model-load) instead of being amortized; p95 for the reranked path is dominated by this cold start, not the actual scoring.
recommendation: Run rerank.py as a long-lived worker/HTTP service that loads the model once and accepts queries over stdin/loopback; reuse the process across calls. Keep a bounded concurrency limit so spawned workers don't exhaust memory.

issue: getTopProducts recomputes a sort over the whole products collection on every homepage load with no caching
evidence: productController.js:154-156 `Product.find({}).sort({ rating: -1 }).limit(3)` — runs an in-memory sort (no index on rating) on every GET /api/products/top, which HomeScreen fires on every default-mode mount
estimated_impact: Without an index on `rating`, Mongo does a collection scan + top-k sort per call. The result is near-static (changes only when reviews change) yet recomputed on every home visit. At modest traffic this is wasted CPU; ~5-30ms per call that could be ~0 from cache.
recommendation: Add an index on `rating` (`-1`) and cache the top-3 result in memory with a short TTL (e.g. 60s), or precompute on review write.

issue: createProductReview reloads, recomputes numReviews and the rating average by re-reducing the entire reviews array on every new review
evidence: productController.js:137-141 `product.numReviews = product.reviews.length; product.rating = product.reviews.reduce(...) / length` then `product.save()` re-serializes the whole embedded reviews array
estimated_impact: As a product accumulates reviews, each new review loads the full reviews subarray into memory, re-reduces it (O(n)), and rewrites the entire document. For a popular product with thousands of embedded reviews this is O(n) CPU + a multi-KB document rewrite per review. Embedded unbounded reviews also bloat every getProductById response (no projection).
recommendation: Maintain a running average incrementally (newRating = (rating*numReviews + r)/(numReviews+1)) and use `$push`/`$inc` atomic updates instead of loading+rewriting the whole document; consider moving reviews to their own collection with pagination if counts grow.
